sections.h2: What kind of county is Dooly County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Dooly County is a rural county in central Georgia with Vienna as its seat. The legislature created it on May 15, 1821, from land ceded by the Creek Nation, and named it for Colonel John Dooly, a Revolutionary War fighter. Crisp County was cut out of its original borders, along with parts of Macon, Pulaski, Turner, Wilcox and Worth counties, so its original borders covered far more ground than today.

Wikipedia reports 397 square miles in the upper Atlantic coastal plain. Most of the western two-thirds drains to the Flint River, the northeast and east drain to the Ocmulgee, and the far southeast corner reaches the Alapaha basin. Neighbors are Houston, Pulaski, Wilcox, Crisp, Sumter and Macon counties.

Lilly, Byromville, Pinehurst, Unadilla and Vienna are the cities, and Dooling, Drayton and Findlay are towns. Unadilla is the largest. The 2020 census counted no urban residents at all, so nearly every sale here is a farm, small-town or acreage property, and the county offices in Vienna handle most steps.

sections.h2: Where are the Dooly County tax offices and what are their hours?
sections.html:
Three county offices matter to a seller, and the first two share a building at 105 W. Cotton Street in Vienna.

The tax commissioner's page also links an online payment portal and a tag renewal link to the Georgia DRIVES site. Because the commissioner's office closes on Fridays, plan any payoff request or in-person payment for Monday through Thursday.

sections.h2: Did Dooly County raise its millage rate for 2025?
sections.html:
The county posted a notice that its commissioners had tentatively adopted a 2025 millage rate requiring a 2.62% increase in property tax revenue. The proposed rate was 17.45 mills, up 0.445 mills, against a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills.

Three public hearings were set at the commissioners' office on 113 N. Third Street: two on Thursday, September 4, at 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., and one on Friday, September 19, at 10:00 a.m. Those hearing dates have passed, so a seller should ask the tax commissioner for the final rate that appears on the current bill. The notice itself worked out two sample increases, about $25.81 for a homestead with a fair market value of $150,000 and about $26.70 for a non-homestead property of the same value.

Georgia sets assessed value at 40 percent of fair market value, and the millage rate applies to that assessed figure. The notice covers the county's own levy; ask the tax commissioner which school and city rates appear on a given parcel's bill.

sections.h2: How does a Dooly County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Begin by phoning the Assessors Office at 229-268-4719. Each year the board mails a notice of assessment, and an owner who rejects the stated fair market value gets 45 days, counted from the mailing date, to file. The postmark has to fall inside that window.

  • Grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption
  • The state's PT-311A form lets you pick a Board of Equalization hearing, a hearing officer or arbitration
  • Email is allowed only if the board has a written policy accepting electronic service
  • Do not send the form to the state revenue department

The notice itself carries the filing instructions, so keep the envelope or note the postmark date. A refund for tax that was erroneously or illegally collected must be requested in writing within three years of payment.

sections.h2: What returns and exemptions apply to Dooly County property?
sections.html:
The county tax office takes returns of value in the first quarter, January 1 to April 1. Silence counts as a repeat of last year's value for anyone who paid then. For homestead, apply once the house is your primary residence and before April 1 of the first benefit year; a missed application forfeits that year.

The Department of Revenue's Dooly page describes the state exemptions without a local add-on, so ask the commissioner whether the county offers anything beyond them. The commissioner's page links a tax information pamphlet with homestead details. Ask the office for a current copy before you rely on older figures.

Voters can also exempt commercial and industrial inventory under the freeport exemption, which is requested from the board of assessors during the return period. That rule affects owners of a shop or warehouse building, not a typical house.

sections.h2: What do mobile home and vehicle rules mean for a Dooly County sale?
sections.html:
Mobile homes follow their own track. State rules call for a location permit from the tax commissioner within 30 days of placement, renewed every year in the first quarter. A mobile home sitting in the county on January 1 is returned for taxation by April 1, together with the permit.

  • A mobile home on land you are selling needs its permit and return current
  • Vehicle registration renews with the commissioner in the 30 days ending on the owner's birthday
  • A newly bought vehicle needs registration within 30 days
  • Only the tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax

Ask the tax commissioner to confirm the status of any mobile home on the parcel before a buyer's lender does.

sections.h2: What taxes come due when a Dooly County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on January 1 carries that whole year's ad valorem tax, even after a spring or summer sale. How the bill is divided is a contract term, and the closing statement should show the proration.

At recording, the seller owes Georgia transfer tax, which the revenue department states as $1 for the first $1,000 of price and 10 cents for each additional $100. A long-term note secured by land adds an intangible recording tax, which the revenue department sets at $1.50 per $500 of face amount, with the security instrument recorded locally inside 90 days. Tax liens, whether county or state, are entered on the clerk's general execution docket.

The usual state due date is December 20 unless the county picks another, and interest waits 60 days after the bill is postmarked. Request a payoff figure from the commissioner for your closing agent.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Dooly County homes?
sections.html:
The 2025 estimate is 11,156 people, off 0.5% since April 2020, living among 4,906 housing units. Builders pulled only 22 permits last year.

  • Owner-occupied share, 2020 to 2024: 64.7%
  • Typical owned-home value: $107,400
  • Median gross rent: $758
  • Median household income: $60,987
  • Residents living in poverty: 25.6%
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.1%
  • Households with broadband: 76.6%

Wikipedia's reading of the 2020 census shows 4,762 housing units with 15.0% vacant, and county population fell from 14,918 in 2010 to 11,208 in 2020.

faqs.q: When is the Dooly County tax office open?
faqs.a: Monday through Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Friday. Find it at 105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1, Vienna, or call 229-268-4212.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a Dooly County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice went in the mail. File in writing with the county board of tax assessors rather than the state, and call 229-268-4719 with questions.

faqs.q: Does Dooly County have a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The state exemption is available, and the revenue department's Dooly page describes no local add-on, so ask the commissioner about anything more. Apply by April 1 of the first year you want it, since a missed application waives that year.

faqs.q: What was Dooly County's proposed 2025 millage rate?
faqs.a: The county's notice proposed 17.45 mills, an increase of 0.445 mills over a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills. Check your current bill with the tax commissioner for the rate in force.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax if my Dooly County house sells midyear?
faqs.a: The person who owned it January 1 is liable for the full year under Georgia law. A contract can pass part to the buyer, so check the proration on the closing statement.
